correctness.rationale: The normalized inexact WRaSK recurrence matches the published Algorithm 1 with \(x_0=y_0=0\), \(\lambda=1/2\). The three integer row vectors have squared lengths \(2,5,2\) and determinant \(-3\). The nine uniform two-step squared errors sum to \(4193/100\), giving \(4193/900\). The row sequence \((2,1)\) has exact squared error \(971/200\). For every real \(p\ge24\) its probability strictly exceeds \((100/101)(2048/2049)\) and the resulting expected-error bound \(994304/206949>4193/900\) proves the reversal. The first-step weighted error strictly decreases because the best row has probability exceeding \(1/3\). For two arbitrary unit rows, \(4(R_g-R_u)=(1+c^2)(u^2-v^2)+2(cu-v)^2\ge0\) whenever \(|u|\ge|v|\) proves a universal non-reversal for unregularized projections, including ties and parallel rows. The exact-fraction verifier replays all critical probabilities, computations and 343 rational identity checks; the general identity, not the finite checks, establishes the universal statement.

originality.rationale: The WRaSK defining publication proves an improving Bregman-distance rate-bound coefficient, not pointwise ordering of true two-step Euclidean squared risks. Steinerberger proves an improved worst-case residual-weighted Kaczmarz contraction bound, not finite-horizon actual-error domination. Nutini et al. and Haddock-Ma analyze greedy or partial-greedy convergence rates, not the specific counterexample nor the exact two-row identity. The 2025 continual-learning task-ordering comparison uses a different task-selection model and performance criteria. Published one-step coherence residual-spike results do not imply this two-step expected solution-error ordering. Matching primary articles and selected original proof sections were examined; negative searches are not a proof of global novelty. The independent 2021 conference treatment by Tondji, Winkler and Lorenz also states the same sparse method and an expected squared-error rate bound, but the full published text offers no exact two-step comparison or row-count barrier. Its first public day is not established from the year-level conference attribution.

value.rationale: Residual-power weighting targets the largest immediate corrections and earlier results prove improved sufficient convergence factors. The explicit source-initialized \(\lambda=1/2\) sparse iteration instead exhibits an exact two-step loss in expected squared error after a strict first-step gain. The all-real \(p\ge24\) statement is proved by a probability bound; the general two-row defect identity establishes that three row labels are minimal for this phenomenon **in unregularized orthogonal-projection Kaczmarz**. This is a motivated finite-budget distinction, not an arbitrary numerical slice; it does not assert a worse asymptotic or typical-case rate.
